judged_text: In updateEvent the fallback branch searches `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` with a falsy `externalCalendarId`, so the lookup can never match and `selectedCalendar` is always undefined in that branch. When updateEvent is invoked without an externalCalendarId (EventManager's updateAllCalendarEvents passes `calenderExternalId` which is null when the booking reference has no stored external id), the previous fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is destroyed and Google's events.update is called with `calendarId: undefined`, causing the update to fail with a 404/bad-request instead of updating the host's calendar event.

When updateEvent is invoked without an externalCalendarId (EventManager's updateAllCalendarEvents passes `calenderExternalId` which is null when the booking reference has no stored external id), the previous fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is destroyed and Google's events.update is called with `calendarId: undefined`, causing the update to fail with a 404/bad-request instead of updating the host's calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the new fallback computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g., `null` as passed from `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` via `calenderExternalId` when no reference external id exists), the `.find(... === externalCalendarId)` can’t match any real `externalId`, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined`. The previous behavior (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, now an array’s first entry) is effectively lost, so Google `events.update` will be invoked without a valid calendar id (unless it has an unseen fallback), likely breaking updates.
